detail.description: Windows 上的 Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 到 6.3.7 向 OpenSSL 提供其自己的 TLS 文件的名称 - 侦听器的证书、链、私钥和 Diffie-Hellman 参数、端口的客户端证书 CA 文件（从 6.2.19 开始）、对象存储的 CA 文件（从 6.3.4 开始）以及 ACME 客户端的密钥和证书 - 作为 Latin-1 字节，位于代码页上1252 是 U+00A0 到 U+00FF 本身的代码页，Windows 上的 OpenSSL 文件打开首先读取 UTF-8 名称，然后在该文件所在的位置打开该文件，或者在其文件夹所在的位置创建该文件。当 ASCII 之外的配置名称的每个字节也读取为 UTF-8 时（例如 U+00C3 U+00A9、字节 C3 A9，在 UTF-8 中为 U+00E9），服务器只要有文件存在，就会使用其他名称的文件，这使得本地攻击者可以创建该文件或其文件夹，但无法更改配置的文件（默认情况下，任何用户都可以在管理员保存在 ProgramData 下的文件旁边），以拥有通过客户端证书（来自6.2.25) 接受来自攻击者自己的证书颁发机构的证书，然后以任何邮箱（无需密码）的身份通过网络登录；让服务器信任其对象存储的此类权限，并拦截该连接，读取和修改它存储的消息；接收ACME客户端写入的私钥，其中为服务器名称颁发的证书的密钥；或者阻止 TLS 端口启动。配置不是默认配置：默认情况下，这些文件的名称采用 ASCII 格式，每个端口上的客户端证书均处于关闭状态，并且对象存储和 ACME 均处于关闭状态。 Linux 版本不受影响。
detail.title: hMailServer 中的证书验证不正确

detail_original.description: Progressive Robot hMailServer 6.0.0-B1 through 6.3.7 on Windows hands OpenSSL the names of its own TLS files - the listeners' certificates, chains, private keys and Diffie-Hellman parameters, a port's client-certificate CA file (from 6.2.19), the object store's CA file (from 6.3.4) and the ACME client's keys and certificates - as Latin-1 bytes, which on code page 1252 are the code page's own for U+00A0 to U+00FF, and OpenSSL's file opening on Windows reads a name as UTF-8 first and opens the file at that reading when it is there, or creates it there when its folder is. When every byte of a configured name outside ASCII also reads as UTF-8 - for example U+00C3 U+00A9, the bytes C3 A9, which are U+00E9 in UTF-8 - the server used the file at that other name whenever one was there, which allows a local attacker who can create that file or its folder but cannot change the configured one, as any user can by default beside a file an administrator keeps under ProgramData, to have a port that logs on by client certificate (from 6.2.25) accept certificates from a certificate authority of the attacker's own and so sign in over the network as any mailbox without its password; to have the server trust such an authority for its object store and, intercepting that connection, read and modify the messages it stores; to receive the private keys the ACME client writes, the key of a certificate issued for the server's names among them; or to keep TLS ports from starting. The configuration is not the default: by default these files have names in ASCII, client certificates are off on every port, and the object store and ACME are off. The Linux builds are not affected.
detail_original.title: Improper Certificate Validation in hMailServer
